  - Words 35–40 are time and place words used in daily speech.

  The README still contains only its title. The table groups 40 basic words by part of speech, and each one has a
  Chinese translation and a usage note.

❯ Without using tools, write 6 short paragraphs about bridges, the second with a numbered list of 3 items and one line
  of inline code.

● Bridges are among the oldest structures people build. From fallen logs laid across streams to steel spans over wide
  bays, they all do the same job: carry people and goods over a gap that would otherwise be hard or impossible to
  cross.

  Engineers usually sort bridges by how they carry loads, and three basic types cover most designs. In a simple model
  you might write the load rule as load_capacity > dead_load + live_load, the requirement every design must meet.
  1. Beam bridges rest a horizontal deck on supports at each end.
  2. Arch bridges push their weight outward along a curve into strong abutments.
  3. Suspension bridges hang the deck from cables slung between tall towers.

  Materials have changed bridge building over the centuries. The Romans used stone and concrete for arches that still
  stand today. The Industrial Revolution brought iron and then steel, which allowed much longer spans. Modern bridges
  often use prestressed concrete and high-strength steel cables.

  Wind and vibration are some of the hardest problems engineers face. The 1940 collapse of the Tacoma Narrows Bridge
  showed how wind can make a deck twist until it fails. After it, aerodynamic testing in wind tunnels became a standard
  part of designing long-span bridges.

  Bridges also carry cultural meaning. The Golden Gate Bridge, Tower Bridge in London and the Zhaozhou Bridge in China
  are landmarks as much as roads. People photograph them, write poems about them, and use them as symbols of connection
  between places and communities.

  Today, bridge engineering puts more weight on long-term maintenance and monitoring. Sensors embedded in decks and
  cables can track strain, temperature and movement in real time. That helps keep these structures safe for decades, so
